links.outcome: Feasibility of retrospective shadow-mode evaluation of LLM antibiotic recommendations on real admissions
links.effect: LLM recommendations generated post hoc, hidden from clinicians, with no influence on care, were evaluated on 493 admissions; guardrail violations 4.9% for LLM vs 17.0% for clinicians.
links.quote: We therefore evaluated whether post hoc LLM-generated empiric antibiotic recommendations showed greater concordance with a pre-specified stewardship benchmarking framework than clinician-initiated regimens in a retrospective shadow-mode setting.

links.outcome: Guardrail violation rate of LLM vs clinician empiric antibiotic regimens on same admissions
links.effect: Violations in 17.0% of clinician regimens vs 4.9% of LLM regimens (paired RD -12.2%; matched OR 0.216, 95% CI 0.127-0.367; McNemar exact p = 1.60 × 10^-10).
links.quote: Guardrail violations occurred in 17.0% of clinician regimens vs. 4.9% of LLM regimens (paired RD -12.2%; matched OR 0.216, 95% CI 0.127-0.367; McNemar exact p = 1.60 × 10-10).

screen.reason: Empirical retrospective evaluation comparing post hoc LLM-generated empiric antibiotic regimens (with structured local epidemiology provided in the prompt context) against clinician prescribing, measuring adherence to prespecified antimicrobial stewardship guardrails.

primary.practice: local epidemiology prompt grounding and rule-based guardrail auditing
